notes.ekika: Oruganda, a clan. Not the same as Luganda Oluganda, the language.
notes.omuziro: A totem: an animal or thing the clan doesn’t eat.
notes.kya: Of, for eki- nouns: ekitabo kya Mukasa.
notes.gwa: Of, for omu- nouns like omuziro.
notes.tetulya: Said of a clan’s totem: we don’t eat it.
notes.jjajja-omutaka: Omukuru w’oruganda, the head of the clan.

guidebook.intro: Every Munyankore belongs to a clan, oruganda, passed down from the father. Each clan has a totem, omuziro, an animal or thing its members must not eat or harm.

tips.title: Oruganda and omuziro
body: Ask someone’s clan with **Ori w’oruganda ki?** (you’re of which clan?) and answer **Ndi wa** + the clan. The totem is **omuziro**, plural **emiziro**: members say **titurya** + the totem (we don’t eat it).
Watch out: Runyankore **oruganda** means clan, while Luganda **Oluganda** is the Luganda language.

tips.title: Of agrees with the first noun
body: “Of” takes the prefix of the noun it follows: **omukuru w’oruganda** (the head of the clan), **ekitabo kya Mukasa** (Mukasa’s book), **ebitabo bya Mukasa** (Mukasa’s books), **emiziro gy’enganda** (the totems of the clans).

culture.title: Ankole clans
body: Well-known Ankole clans include the **Abahinda**, the royal clan, and the **Abashambo**, **Abagahe** and **Abasingo**. Members of the same clan are family and may not marry each other.
